comparator.name: Future Planet Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The official February 2026 chart gives a 60 EC shared first year, 15 EC shared and 45 EC major-specific in year 2, and 30 EC elective space plus 30 EC of required project and research work in year 3. The generic target offers two equally formal majors. Future Earth is shown because it is listed first on the official programme page. Its plant–soil, ecological and spatial study leads into water management and desertification fieldwork. Research Designs accompanies the Bachelor Project.

alternatives.label: Earth systems, food & water sustainability
alternatives.concept: Study climate, Earth systems, soils, ecosystems, food and water. Use spatial and statistical methods to investigate environmental change and examine how policy choices affect communities.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule follows the selected Future Earth route through Earth systems, ecology, soils, food, water and environmental research while retaining the programme's shared societal dimension.
progression: Sustainability, biodiversity and economics precede spatial observation, soils, sustainable farming and water. Biogeochemistry, marine biology, statistics and governance extend these foundations. Current offerings and prerequisites pass.
traceOverrides: examines circular resource use, recovery and remediation within an integrated sustainability programme
examines resource and environmental challenges through advanced Earth-system research

alternatives.label: Environmental governance & just transitions
alternatives.concept: Study how institutions and communities respond to climate change and manage environmental resources. Combine Earth systems and water study with politics, law, public economics and climate communication.
alternatives.labelReason: The official Future Society direction supplies the organising logic; governance, politics, law, environmental justice and climate communication form the scheduled focus.
progression: Sustainability and comparative politics precede international relations and justice. The law gateway precedes public international law. Spatial analysis, water, public economics, civil society and advanced politics support applied governance. Current offerings and prerequisites pass.
alternatives.distinctness: 9 courses and 67.5 EC differ in each direction relative to UCR option 1.
traceOverrides: examines circular resource use, recovery and remediation as a sustainability-governance problem
provides advanced Earth-resource evidence for environmental governance decisions

alternatives.label: Energy transitions & sustainable enterprise
alternatives.concept: Study renewable energy, circular material use and resource management. Combine environmental science and system design with economics, market research and organisational change.
alternatives.labelReason: The required Energy Transitions theme and its related energy, technology and policy subjects support this composition. Business and leadership courses add ways to study how organisations can implement transitions.
progression: Sustainability, business, economics and methods precede circular design and renewable systems. Market research and econometrics follow the relevant business and methods foundations. Current offerings and prerequisites pass.
alternatives.distinctness: 9 courses and 67.5 EC differ in each direction relative to UCR option 1. 10 courses and 75 EC differ in each direction relative to UCR option 2.
traceOverrides: establishes climate-system and transition foundations for the energy-and-enterprise programme
uses GIS and remote-sensing evidence to evaluate environmental change and sustainable projects

routeSelection.basis: The generic target has two equally formal majors, Future Earth and Future Society. Neither is identified as broader, less specialised or more representative of the overall bachelor, so the first-listed Future Earth major is selected from the current official 2026-2027 curriculum before considering UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The broad Future Earth response, a governance composition grounded in Future Society, and an energy-transition composition grounded in the required energy theme are coherent and feasible. Each pair has at least 30 EC of distinct study, reaching the maximum of three UCR alternatives.

blocks: Earth systems, climate, ecosystems, food and water
Both introduce complex sustainability challenges and systems thinking; the UvA course includes a first academic paper.
Both examine Earth-system processes. UCR concentrates on geology and geophysics, while UvA also integrates biology and chemistry.
Both examine climate-system processes, impacts, sea-level change and societal responses.
Both address ecosystems and biodiversity; the UvA course connects global biomes explicitly to food supply.
Both address natural hazards and their impacts. UvA explicitly uses Google Earth Pro to study spatial patterns.
Both develop remote-sensing and spatial-data methods for environmental change.
Both study soil properties and their environmental significance; the UvA course focuses specifically on plant-soil relations in food systems.
Both critically examine sustainable alternatives to industrial agriculture.
Both study water availability, hydrological processes, management and adaptation.
The compulsory Future Earth laboratory and field practical has no single ordinary UCR equivalent.
Both study aquatic life and ecosystems. Marine Biology concentrates on marine settings; UvA explicitly connects aquatic science, human impacts and restoration.
The preparatory environmental-data course tied to the Desertification field course has no separate UCR equivalent.
The dedicated field course in geo-ecological mapping and desertification has no single ordinary UCR equivalent.
Both design responses to water-related sustainability challenges. UvA explicitly teaches scenario planning, while Building with Nature explores design using natural processes.
Both examine how science, politics, institutions and society shape sustainability transitions.
Both consider how environmental conditions affect communities. UCR focuses on social movements and environmental justice; UvA takes a broader quality-of-life perspective.
Both address externalities, public policy and welfare. UvA focuses directly on environmental pollution and climate economics.
Both compare energy sources and transitions through technical, economic and environmental perspectives.
Data, research, projects and open space
Both teach research design. UvA’s course supports the parallel Bachelor Project, while UCR’s course introduces empirical design and statistics.
Both use R to work with and visualise data. UvA also introduces formal statistical inference.
Both develop statistical models, uncertainty estimation and hypothesis testing.
UvA requires a collaborative interdisciplinary coastal project. UCR includes applied methods and field study across several courses.
The dedicated group research course combining interviews and surveys around quality of life has no single ordinary UCR equivalent.
The compulsory programme-specific philosophy-of-science course has no single course in these UCR schedules.
The dedicated R programming course has no separate ordinary-course equivalent in these UCR schedules.
The genuine 30-EC elective semester remains student-selected and is not a fixed external course to align.
The compulsory 18-EC individual Bachelor Project cannot be counted as an ordinary UCR course or as UCR's optional comparison-only research element.

notes.text: UvA combines semester challenges with a 45 EC major, specialist field and laboratory work, and an 18 EC Bachelor Project. UCR covers related environmental and societal questions across separate courses. The table shows Future Earth as the UvA route.

audience.programmeDescription: Future Planet Studies at the University of Amsterdam brings natural and social sciences together to study climate, energy, food and water. Students choose Future Earth or Future Society in year two and complete an individual research project in year three.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines Earth science, ecology, soils and water with environmental methods and policy. The other options focus on environmental governance or on energy transitions and enterprise.

componentNotes.y2-digital-earth: Students prepare and analyse environmental datasets for use in the Desertification field course.
componentNotes.y3-open: Choose 30 EC of electives, a minor or study abroad.
componentNotes.y3-bachelor-project: Complete an individual research project in the major. Research Designs supports the proposal and final report.
